About the Program
Smart Agriculture Energy Innovation Network

SAGEIN is a $3 million NSF Research Traineeship at Mississippi State University integrating engineering, agriculture, human sciences, and economics to address the intertwined challenges of energy, food, and rural economic development. The traineeship program begins Fall 2026.

Students from engineering, agriculture, economics, computer science, environmental science, data science, and related disciplines are all encouraged to apply. No prior energy background required.

Quick Facts

Award:NSF NRT No. 2510164
Amount:$3,000,000
Period:Sep 1, 2025 – Aug 31, 2030
Starts:Fall 2026 at MSU
PI:Dr. Tonya W. Stone
Co-PIs:Dr. Gang Li, Dr. Jay McCurdy, Dr. Carley Morrison, Dr. Jian Zhao
Certificate:12 credit hours · 1 year

Distributed Energy Systems

Rural DRES assessment, design, and management — solar, wind, bioenergy, and storage

Smart Agriculture

Agrivoltaics, precision ag, IoT-enabled resource management, and field-based innovation

AI & Decision Support

Machine learning, time-series forecasting, and AI-driven energy optimization tools

Rural Community Engagement

Direct collaboration with MSU Extension, county agents, farmers, and rural producers

Graduate Certificate
Interdisciplinary Certificate Program

Open to graduate students across engineering, agriculture, economics, computer science, environmental science, data science, human sciences, and natural resources. Students bring expertise from their home department and develop convergent skills alongside peers from different fields — one year, 12 credit hours, designed to complement your existing MS or PhD program.

  • Real-world rural energy assessments with farmers, Extension partners, and community stakeholders
  • Interdisciplinary training alongside peers from engineering, agriculture, economics, and beyond
  • AI and IoT skills for distributed energy optimization and precision agriculture
  • Entrepreneurship, intellectual property, and technology transfer training
  • Summer placement opportunities at Pacific Northwest National Laboratory and industry partners
  • A competitive credential aligned with NSF national workforce priorities in Clean Energy, Biotechnology, and AI

NRT Traineeship Fellowship

$37,000
Annual Stipend + 1 Year Tuition Support

Competitive fellowship positions are available for eligible MS and PhD students. All applicants use a single form — simply check the fellowship box to be considered.

How to Apply
Apply to SAGEIN
1
Talk to your advisor
Get written approval confirming the certificate aligns with your degree plan and research progress.
2
Complete the application
Submit the form including a 500–750 word Statement of Purpose describing your interest and career goals.
3
Indicate fellowship interest
Check the fellowship box on the form to be considered for the $37,000 annual stipend and tuition support.
4
Submit by July 1
Applications for the Fall 2026 cohort are due July 1.
Questions? Contact Ms. Santee Ezell at se126@msstate.edu
